review:
"Over? Oh it's not over until I teabag every last one of you alien mother f***ers" - Sam 'Serious' Stone, Serious Sam 3

THE GOOD
The Serious Sam series has always been an antidote to the shooters which may or may not have a player character who kills off people who are different to them because they look different, sound different and speak different languages, in where you have a whole lot of aliens trying to trample and shoot you from all sides, just like the 4:17pm on December 24th. There weren't any key card quests, no escort missions, and no real story which was involing in any way. The gameplay may turn off hardcore Serious Sam fans for the first few levels. Few enemies will attack you systematically while you kill them off in a straight line. After you reach the Shpynx however, it starts to hit the fans and the aliens who outnumber the amount of Steam gamers with light wallets will charge and generally blow you to pieces. Just like the good old days.

THE GREAT
Remember when you realised that you could play co-op on some of your favourite games? It was the dogs bollocks (Pretty satisfying) wasn't it? Whatever gamemode that has co-op elements in this kicks all kinds of alien ass, and there's nothing more enjoyable than decapitating a demon which you woke from it's slumber with something that resembles a laser whip from Star Wars. Be it Beast Hunt, Coin Op or just straight out Classic Co-op, it will be a helluva good time, especially with the customisation involved in it.

THE UGLY
Croteam, we love your level design. Serious Sam TFE and TSE were fantastic! We'll blame SS2 on the annoying child that kept pestering you on the next Serious Sam game who said that his father/older sibling played it and he wasn't allowed to. At least you regained your thing with the singleplayer in this. For the most part. The first few levels have you going through corridors killing off enemies not for fun, but simply because they're in the way. There is little reason to like the first few levels for many people, which will turn off some players. Later into the campaign you get cannons and miniguns and so on, so fourth, but here's a comparrison. In the first level of TFE, you get a rocket launcher, a double barralled shotgun, a single barralled shotgun, you fight off biomechs and witch harpies (If you find all the secrets at least). In the first level of TSE, you get a rocket launcher, both shotguns, a sniper, a chainsaw and a flamethrower while killing witch harpies, arachnids and lumberjacks with pumpkins for heads weilding chainsaws. And the best you find in BFE is a shotgun, some ammo for the assualt rifle and a few kleers and gnarrs? I know which I prefer. Also, a few mechanics like sprinting, aiming and reloading have been redundantly been introduced, but those are mostly optional, so not too bad.

THE VERDICT
Overall not a bad game. Worth getting on sale, but do not judge the game on the story and the singleplayer alone. If you get through to the sixth or seventh level, it will ramp things up a bit. And that's a promise.

SIMILAR GAMES
-Any first person shooter from Id Software before 1999
-Painkiller and Serious Sam TSE

Its not as engaging as original First and Second Encounters. BUT still lot of fun especially Co-op. Survival is also fun. Return to a more realistic Egypt than TFE. Lots of hard new enemies. Nice new weapons. Lots of breakable structures. Last Boss level is kickass too. I just miss good old Serious Bomb, Flame Thrower, Serious Speed, the funky booby trapped secrets, funky secret areas and Rocket Jump. And yeah no sewage level this time. That said I am sure I had posted a review before so why is it asking again a review? 

I miss the crazy anti-gravity maps. The anti-gravity mode is only seen in final climax bossfight. The graphics is top notch. Gameplay and action as usual fast and smooth. As usual both the solo and co-op campaigns are same with various difficulty and modes/mods available to make gameplay challenging, fun, insanely hard or a run through picnic. Take your pick. Thats consistent with all Sam games. 

The new enemies leave a mixed feeling at expense of many classic ones. I find the venomous spiders more a let down compared to missing Aludran Reptiloids, Fiendian Reptiloid Demon, Cucurbito Pumpkin Heads etc. Khnum introduced as a boss in TSE DLC is not so hard to kill here. The wrist Mutilator is most awesome edition though replacing standard chainsaw. But I miss mowing the Kleers / Gnaars with Chainsaw. The level designs just don't feel big and epic enough like original encounters. Maybe needed more enemies and waves smartly placed. Or maybe we expect more bigger levels every new game. The game delivers great cinematic experience and fighting but misses some classic modes, enemies and battles that made it the standard. The Survival levels have 2 brilliant maps Canyon and Desert. Medina and Villa is beatable. Overall have a blast. Play with friends in coops that is usually a run through marathon contest. In original encounters many used rocket jumps to spoil the coop fun for others to end games and run through early. That wont happen here. Most people here don't know the get around shortcuts so well and good. 

I still give it a solid 7.5/10 despite my pointed points on what I miss. The Jewel of Nile DLC is actually better. I would have given it 8.5  but i really did not like underground repetetive tombs in cramped spaces much. Would have been fun in one or 2 levels not half the game. I understand thats expected in actual Egypt tombs still.....Thats why the DLC scores, less dark tombs more open spaces with big waves.

I love all the Serious Sam games to date, I used to play them as a child and really enjoyed them, thats why I have a lot of confronted feelings about this game, so here it goes:

++PROS++
-Mindlessly killing hordes of monsters is always fun
-Not serious game/dialogue, funny one-liners

--CONS--
-It gets TOO repetitive. Dont get me wrong, killing hordes of enemies is fun... but there is a point, where you are in a zone and enemies keep respawning, and killing them stops being fun an becomes a chore. Near the end of the game there is a section where you have to kill around 3000 enemies of all kinds, which takes you like an hour, all in the same place.

-The enviroments: It tried too hard to have "realistic" maps, I mean, with a lot of detailed textures and real-world looking. In my opinion Serious Sam does good with less "serious" textures (which, by the way, dont look that good) and a more cartoony look. Half of the game seems to take place in the same city map and the other half in the same desert map.

-The enemies: 85% of the enemies are the same from older games. This isnt a bad thing of course, but the new enemies they added are completely unoriginal and not fun to fight against. Alien soldiers that have human guns and just stand there shooting at you, also, they dont have projectiles you can dodge, but hitscan, which means that you cant dodge their shots. Wellp, imo that goes a bit against what serious sam is supposed to be.

I had some fun with the game and enjoyed it at the beginning, but it got repetitive real quick and finishing it was kind of boring.
Wouldnt recommend this game for full price.

Seriously one of the best co-op shooters in Steam. While the story has not ever been so important in Serious Sam games I think that this storyline had something serious to tell time to time. The cut scenes are great and balsy and make it clear that Sam is the man to call when mankind makes its last moves against ultimate destruction.

I found SS3 very good in Single Player in small sessions, but it is the co-op when things reach their full potential. I beat this game in a group of 3 to 4 players and oh boy such fun it was. Sadly the main game lasts only about 5-6 hours.

In addition of the gameplay lifetime - the another thing for which I was dissapointed was the lack of drivable vechiles because in SS2 they had them included and they worked as a nice variation. Comeback in Serious Sam 4? Nevertheless, other cool feautres like a large weapon arsenal and attacking enemies in large hordes are there and I must say that the optimization is pretty good when concidering the high quality graphics. I didn't get any lag on high settings while I was attacked by dozens of alien freaks at the same time. Of course the game is relatively old but so is my current pc.  All this killing frenzy is crowned with an awesome soundtrack which puts the adrenaline flowing.

So if you like co-op or shooters or perhaps both you really got yourself a good deal here maybe not in its full price but in sale at least. Also keep an eye on other installments as well because there is no weakest link in this serious series.

Note: This game been tried out and reviewed in Steam offline mode or on Consoles.

The first Serious Sam, well as its Second Encounter, had everything you could want in an FPS and easy difficulty making you feel invincible - the opposite one teaching you to dodge in realistically deadly scenarios, intense and frantic action with beautiful and detailed level designs and atmosphere, and gigantic environments littered with some crazy secrets. Overall: Sam 3 is an amazing game from indie company-Croteam.This is definitely a good fps game, especially for a Single-player experience. It starts out crazy enough.

The first few levels of the campaign introduce some weapons, treat you to a few enemies at a time, growing into larger and larger waves coming at you at once.

And then holy shit.
Some switch just fucking flips. They go insane. Hordes and hordes of enemies fill the screen, firing, screaming, exploding in your face.

And what do you do?

You kill them all.

If you are looking for an all-out slaughterhouse of a game, this is the one.

If you are new to Serious Sam,PLEASE do not start with this one,this one may look decent but in reality it`s a bit dull looking,especially to it`s older brothers.
Try "The First Encounter" and "The Second Encounter" first before playing this then you might enjoy it.
I did this mistake years ago,making me avoid the series at all.

However,if you already played the previous games you may or not enjoy this one,there are some things I want to talk about in particular:

Pros:
-Enemies design looks dope as hell

-Execution/Glory kill system which looks cool most of the time

-Sprinting,especially useful when hordes of enemies are around all the angles and you can evade most of the time.

-Weapon sound design,they deliver a powerful blow to the enemy especially the shotguns

-The OST is still great to hear,even the main menu theme

Cons:
-Hitscan enemies
Scorpions were a good enemy in the previous games and they hit/miss you even if you sat still in one place.
Now they seem to shoot you perfectly almost all the time. Same thing with shotgun/rifle soldiers.
And the worst one of the hitscan imo is the "Tentacle helicopter" which flies very high and until your rockets fly it gets away so you better hide and run.

-Bride Witch
The worst enemy in this game by far,not only that it`s hard to spot her,especially when you have hordes of kleers,kamikazes,biomechanoids following you only to wake up unable to move and this bitch puts you in the air as well. She can also reflects projectiles which is even worse. 

-The levels are bland looking for the most part
Remember the magic that TFE and TSE and how many memorable levels they had,well,this game barely has any memorable level,maybe the last 2-4 levels but other than those,the rest of them are boring or tedious to complete.

-Reloading
The other games only had the revolvers (let`s be honest,you barely use them anyway) and the double barrel shotgun,they replaced my lovely tommygun with an generic assault rifle which has iron sights as well,and you need to reload it

-Sam
I despise this Sam at all,he may had corny and cheesy one liners in the previous games but at least most of them were good. Here Croteam decided to recycle most of his one liners from TFE/TSE instead of making new ones. Or the fact that most of his one liners are just:
"MOTHERFUCKER"
"FUCK"
"SHIT"

-The atmosphere
TFE and TSE had the perfect atmosphere with being funny at times and at other times more serious (pun not intended),sadly BFE suffers from it as it tries too hard to be serious but in reality it`s just boring.


Conclusion: If you are a fan of Serious Sam or just arena shooters you`ll still enjoy some of this game,but I heavily recommend playing co-op with a friend to get through the levels.

I've given this game way too many chances and yet it failed to do anything even remotely positive with these chances.
Serious Sam 3: BFE is what happens when developers decide to copy trends instead of sticking to what they know best. Sprinting, reloading, EVEN MORE HITSCAN ENEMIES - all of these are just symptoms of a soulless game that doesn't care about the SS franchise legacy and wants to appeal to a bunch of CoD loving Xbox players.
 One of the first things you'll notice is the absolutely terrifying amount of badly designed enemies. Hitscan enemies, such as Scorpions, have always been a pain in the ass but were used sparingly, unlike grunts and choppers in BFE. Grunts are actually hard to spot in the clusterfuck of chaos happening on your screen and choppers are immune to bullet damage, making it so they can be reliably destroyed with only a single weapon. The worst example of this is during a late game mission, when Sam loses his weaponry and has to take on choppers using the rocket launcher. A sequence like this happens twice and the second time the chopper is way to high to be reliably hit with rockets, yet it retains it's accuracy. It's easy to waste all of your rockets trying to hit this shit while being shot at by the big scorpions in the distance.
 Then you get the newly added monkey-like enemies that only appear in certain places where columns are present - they're designed to be killed with a wrist attachment you get earlier and serve as nothing but an annoyance. They are the only enemy in the whole main game line up I decided not to fight at all - it's just annoying and tedious.
 On top of that they decided to add a "stun-based" enemy, that makes controlling the character impossible, juggles Sam in the air and blurs his vision. Did I mention the enemy is flying and can appear in any place in the air? Or that you can only deal certain amount of damage during it's attack cycle, making it so you can't deal with it instantly? 
 For some reason developers decided to make Laser and Sniper Rifle secret only weapons. Meaning ammunition for them can be found almost exclusively in secret stashes and only in small amounts. The game also has a glory kill mechanic, that does NOT make it so you can't be damaged during the animation, rendering it utterly useless in almost any situation.

 Honestly, I could rant about this mess for hours. Be that poorly designed locations (such as the second level) or horrible visibility (urban environments are not suited for the SS gameplay and enemies simply blend in), Serious Sam 3: Before First Encounter just tries to appease the kind of demographic that doesn't care about Serious Sam at all. If you're a fan of older games - skip 3 and 4 (Siberian mayhem is okay), you won't lose much. If you simply stumbled upon this game, then stumble upon a different one.

 I honestly don't understand how a game can be so confused about what it tries to be.
Shame. Real shame.

У цих іграх присутній непереможний герой Сем, який своєю харизмою знищує мільярди монстрів, які викидають на нього на кожному рівні. Before the First Encounter (though Battle For Endor sounds much better!) is the 3rd instalment of Croteam's Serious Sam franchise, however, this time the Croatian guys picked the make-it-a-prequel-it-is-catchier road. To be honest, I have no idea what makes it a prequel - story-wise, you still keep shooting at various aliens until every one of them dies.

The concept is similar to what Painkiller has: you walk / run along and enjoy the silence and suddenly you hear loud music indicating the oncoming hordes, and I mean HORDES, of enemies. Once you are done with all of them you can proceed to the next section - by only hearing your footsteps - where everything starts over.

Your guns are big, using them is very enjoyable and none have the option to be reloaded. You just keep pressing the button until you run out of ammo. Oh, and sometimes there are bigger enemies that are meant to be the bosses. Simple as that.

So, the core elements remained the same: it has always been a mindless shooter with Sam trying to sound as cool as Duke Nukem. My opinion is: sometimes he gets it right and sometimes he doesn't. 

Unlike previous instalments this game looks stunningly beautiful and even though it is already a 3-year old game it requires some high-end components so that you can enjoy the spectacle of blown up enemies and flying body parts!

For those who love this genre (or more like: subgenre) Serious Sam is a must!

Serious Sam 3: BFE

+ The menus are accessible, the opportunities beyond the single player game are impressive, and the game runs smoothly throughout.
+ (GRAPHICS) There's a sense of environmental deja-vu and less high-end beauty than in many of today's top shooters. But for monsters and monstrous levels of death and destruction, Sam 3 is where it's at.
+ (SOUND) Great swells of industrial metal music, crazily verbal enemies, bombastic bombs, and audible gore galore. What's not to like?
+ Serious Sam is a wave-based, run-backwards-while-shooting, roller-coaster of doom from start to finish. Variety is not its strong suit, but more weapon/ammo availability should be.

TL;DR version: Dumb design decisions make this game the weakest in the series so far and immeasurably less enjoyable than previous entries.

Long version: After owning this game since the year it launched, I have finally finished it in time for SS4's recent release. Frankly, it was a soul-crushing experience.

I get how Serious Sam works. I have played through all of the main series up to this one and usually I love the formula. Huge, colourful environments, vast hordes of monsters and an arsenal with all the firepower you need to blast through these challenges. Apart from a few moments of joy, SS3:BFE unfortunately stumbles too often to be a thoroughly enjoyable experience.

Here's a run down of what spoiled this game for me:

- Weapon reloading: Does NOT fit in the Serious Sam formula and adds a lot of clumsiness to the large battles. Have fun taking a few seconds to reload your assault rifle with six kleer skeletons all up in your grill!

- Drab environments: The crumbling present-day Egypt setting looks lifted from any other generic Modern Warfare clone. Gone are the gorgeous vistas of previous games.

- Dust effects: Half the time you can't see the hordes of enemies rushing at you because explosions cause large, completely opaque clouds of dust to rise

- Unbalanced item placement: You will usually be vastly under-resourced. I actually had to run through the last quarter of the penultimate level because the game simply does not provide the ammo you need to blast all the monsters.

- So many hit-scanners!: Way too many enemies use hit-scan weapons and they seem to have extremely long-range, so you spend a lot of time watching your health and armour deplete with little you can do about it. The all-seeing helicopters that fly overhead with their super accurate chainguns can seriously p*ss off!

I wish I liked this game. I finished it out of respect for the series and Croteam, but I'm really hoping these poor design decisions have been addressed in SS4.

Let's be honest, Serious Sam 3: BFE is not the next chapter we hoped for - it has pacing issues, balancing issues, movement issues, a serious shortage of one liners, and quite frankly it just feels bland, with very inconsistent visuals. Seeing as how it is a prequel leading up to Sam traveling back in time, a slow start is understandable, but the game never really picks up the pace until the last two or three levels and keeps throwing only a handful of enemies at the player at a time. Waiting for the next batch of aliens to spawn is all too common. In fact, the spawn rate is so slow that the double barrel shotgun is as effective as an assault rifle for keeping back most waves, and I found myself moving on to the next area before all of the monsters have spawned in. The campaign is far too easy, and most of the locations feel empty, with tons of ammo and no one to shoot. Serious difficulty? I think not.

The amount of basic ammo for shotguns, assault rifle, and explosives is nowhere near proportional to the amount of enemies, and yet sniper rifle bullets and laser gun cells are absent entirely, obtainable only through secret areas and in miniscule amounts, making both weapons utterly useless. It would have been much better to omit them entirely. Many of the said secret areas require "parkour" skills to get to, and highlight serious flaws with the movement system as obstacles and walls often "push" the player away and make navigating narrow ledges and hidden steps needlessly painful.

Exploring levels for secrets also reveals the ugly underbelly of the game. Literally. Around every corner are unfinished, glaring holes that expose the white space beyond the edge of the map. It is just lazy level design that makes one wonder if anyone even looked at the final product before shipping the game. The Sirian installations are supposed to be awe-inspiring technological wonders of a far more advanced civilization, but look like something put together by a novice level designer - identical large empty rooms with terrible reflective textures. Blunders like these are especially obvious in contrast to the rest of the game, which looks beautiful at times. Character animations notwithstanding. Homogeneous enemy waves also jump out as another design flaw, with very few instances of mixed, complementary, enemy types attacking together like in prior games.

That is where the Jewel of the Nile really shines and delivers everything that we have come to know and love about Serious Sam games. Level design is much more interesting, diverse, and well laid out. Difficulty ramps up and enemies attack together, in much greater numbers, making ammo shortages a common occurrence and each encounter a much more strategic affair that requires the player to stay mobile and count every shot. Laser gun and sniper rifle ammunitions finally make an appearance and they are glorious, glorious weapons. Common Reptiloids return as well, as do copious amounts of one-liners. The DLC is what the entire game should have been like and is worth buying the game just for the three levels alone. It's a shame that the boss fight is still just as terrible as in the base game though, but don't let this overly negative review keep you from playing this great game. It may not be the next chapter we hoped for, but it is still a seriously fun game.

I do not recommend this game for various reasons. I'll be talking about a few key features that really wrecked the gameplay. But first, let me tell you that I've been playing the Serious Sam series since I was a kid and always loved it.

I got the game and started playing. But something wasn't right. It didn't feel like Serious Sam. Not at all. I kept on playing, telling myself that it's gotta be worth it. But every minute of it was painful. Killing every enemy became a choir. When I finally got to the final boss, I was so bored and tired that I simply used cheat codes to finish the game.
After that, I sat down and took a long look at the game, trying to figure out what dragged a game with such potential to the ground.


The weapons:

The weapons seem to fit the game. But one feature does not; "Reloading". The reloading feature added to the shotgun and the M4 is the stupidest thing anyone could ever think of. In a game like Serious Sam where you're constantly firing at enemies coming from every direction the last thing you need to do is reload. Never in the previous games where you forced to reload your weapons except for the Revolvers (which doesn't matter because you only used them for a short period at the start of the game) and the Sniper Rifle (which was for balancing). The M4 is like the new Tommy gun and we all know how much we had to use that gun, and yet here we are stuck with a 40 round mag and reloading option. Same goes with the shotgun that holds 8 rounds. This may help the game become realistic but Serious Sam was never about being realistic. You were dropped hundreds of years back only to find lasers and rocket launchers in ancient Egypt, Aztec, Perspolis and etc. It was just about the fun.

The Sledgehammer: There was always something fun about using the Combat Knife or the Chainsaw back in SS1. Both of which felt good when using. SS3 tried to replace them with a new one. It brought the Sledgehammer and the use of Glory kills (which I will talk about further below). The Sledgehammer was never fun for me to use. Using the Right-Click attack would sometimes not hit and force you to always use the Left Click for ensured hits. And the Spin-Around option activated by the R key was the most worthless thing ever. If you're a real SS player, you would barely be surrounded by enemies from more than one direction to even NEED to use this feature. And when you do, it's a hit and miss. It will hit some of the enemies and will also miss some of them. Worse part is you're completely vulnerable during this period and believe me, it will cost you a lot of Health Points. Even pulling it off does not give you a good feeling.

Glory Killing: The feature where you can kill enemies with your bare hands (which I will refer to by Glory Kill from now on) is cool but not welcome in SS. Just because other games do this doesn't mean you should too. It barely fits into the gameplay. Crushing baby spiders and ripping their mother's shell off not only gets repetitive very quickly but also destroys any challenge they would provide. Same goes for most other enemies such as the Gnarr, baby arachnoids and Cloned Riflemen. It just doesn't fit into the SS gameplay at all.

Hit scanning enemies: Hit scanning is a term used for weapons that hit their targets just as they fire. Like most of the guns in different games (such as Counter-Strike). They do not have projectiles that have to travel to their enemies. Hit scanning can be very annoying in a game like SS where there are dozens of enemies on screen all attacking you. In SS1 the only hit scanning enemy was the Arachnoid which made them one of the top priorities to take out. But they were also the only hit scanning enemies and the developers chose that way because they knew the effects of hit scanning. But apparently in SS3 the developers don't give a sh*t about the basics. Now we have Cloned Rifleman who hit scan you with Rifles and Shotguns and usually the game throws AT LEAST a dozen of them at you at once. And because they are hit scanning there's no way to dodge their bullets. All you can do is take cover behind a wall which is NOT something you should see in a SS game.
Also other enemies who DO fire projectiles have very fast projectile speed. Making them too hard to dodge. Might as well make them hit-scan too. Seriously, compare projectile speeds in SS3 and SS1 with each other and see what I mean.

Witch-Bride of Achriman: The last thing you should do in a SS game is to stop moving and stand still. Every player who plays SS for at least half an hour will know this. But apparently the Developers thought it would be a good idea to make an enemy who freezes you where you are and damages you. And the only time you could damage that enemy would be when you are frozen. When she grabs you with her telekinesis powers, you cannot move and will be slightly lifted up in the air. Making you vulnerable to every enemy in sight. In this period anything and anyone can attack you. This is by far the stupidest feature in the game.

HUD color and size: In the previous SS games the color of different things provided in your HUD were different to help you quickly recognize them. Health and Armor color differed. Ammo types differed. They all differed in color to help you recognize them quick in the heat of the battle without taking much time and their different sizes also helped. Health and Armor were bigger than ammo stocks and your score were the smallest texts.
In SS3 however, everything provided in the HUD is white and they are all the same size. Making it hard and annoying to read them in the middle of a battle. While in previous games it would take you a very quick glance at your HUD to realize everything, it now takes at least a second to do the same.

The Kleer: The Kleer have always been of the most iconic and also most annoying enemies in the SS series. Killing them has always been a pain. However in SS2 they slowed down their movement speed and projectile speed making them a much more player friendly. Now you don't hate them as much and they seem to be as much fun killing as other enemies. In SS3, the developers forgot about this and decided that they should instead make them faster. So here we are, the Kleers now have more health than before and have faster movement and projectiles speed. They are now the one of the most annoying enemies to encounter.

Dark Tombs: It is now very common to go into underground tombs were there is no source of light and be forced to use your flashlight in areas that all look alike and also fight enemies in them. The flashlight is bad. You stand in a giant rectangle or square tomb with pillars in it and every wall looks the same as the other one. And you are usually forced to check every wall for an entry which looks exactly the same on every wall. Your flashlight has a range so you can't see the other end of the room. You'll find yourself constantly walking from wall to wall trying to figure out which one you have to enter and once you do, you pull a lever that opens a door on the other walls which again you have to search for. This becomes even more annoying with the new added cave demons.

Aurigan Cave Daemons: Serious Sam is all about pace and game speed. You are constantly encouraged to keep moving and get to the next area. But in SS3 this is completely broken with the newly added enemy; the cave daemons. They are monkey like enemies who strap onto the many pillars in the dark tombs and face away from the player, all camping and waiting to lunge at the player after he looks away. So killing them is always a choir. They force you to spend 5 minutes just running around trying to find and kill them. It doesn't help that their color is also black, completely hiding them in the dark.


I had high hopes for this game but it's saddens me to say that it is the WORST entry in the game series. I cannot recommend it even to the most hardcore SS player. Save your money and don't buy this cr*p.

Serious Sam 3: BFE was positioned as a return to the roots, a prequel to the original The First Encounter. However, instead of a brisk step back, we got a stumbling, tedious walk through a sun-scorched desert. The game, which promised adrenaline-pumping action, ultimately feels more like running with weights on your legs.

Right from the start, the contrast with the previous installments is striking. There, we were thrown into colorful alien landscapes full of insane action. Here, we have monotonous and boring locations inspired by Egypt. Brown walls, sand dunes, and rare, but monotonous ruins – that's the whole visual attraction. Where are the explosive colors of the Croatian countryside? Where are the cyberpunk cities full of neon? Alas, all of this is completely absent in Serious Sam 3.

As for the gameplay, there are also problems here. The game certainly tries to return to the roots, but it does so too literally. The enemies, of course, come in hordes, but their variety leaves much to be desired. Plus, they have a "growl" before attacking, which, it would seem, should give the player time to react. In reality, it only irritates, interrupting the continuous flow of action that was the hallmark of the series. Instead of a chaotic ballet of death, we get a jerky, uneven shootout.

The weapons, of course, remained recognizable and powerful, but their use seems less effective than before. The increased difficulty doesn't help either. The game has become not just difficult, but unfairly difficult. Constant deaths from unexpected attacks and endless crowds of enemies appearing literally out of nowhere quickly lead to frustration. Instead of the fun destruction of alien scum, we are engaged in the monotonous shooting of the same mobs, hoping to survive until the next checkpoint.

Attempts to add "seriousness" to the game in the form of a pseudo-realistic plot and characters also seem inappropriate. "Serious Sam" has always been a parody of action movies, not the action movie itself. Attempts to make Sam a "cool guy" seem strained and ridiculous. His jokes, which used to bring a smile, now seem flat and unfunny.

In the end, Serious Sam 3: BFE is a disappointing return to the roots that ended in a painful fall. The game suffers from monotonous locations, a meager set of enemies, irritating difficulty, and clumsy attempts to add "seriousness" to it. If you are looking for crazy and adrenaline-pumping action like in the previous installments, then Serious Sam 3, unfortunately, will not meet your expectations. It's better to replay the old games of the series - they still give odds to this prequel.

As much as it pains me to say, as a Serious Sam fan, the third game... is just ain't it.
For those who don't know - Serious Sam 3 is a combination of a cancelled vanilla military shooter set in the Middle East (as seen by the level design and most weapons) and a DOOM 4 prototype (a design for the Scrapjack enemy can be a proof of that) and of course, Serious Sam.
Some mechanics from the scrapped military shooter made their way to the gameplay loop, for instance:
- ADS with weapons
- Sprinting
- Reloading
- Hit-scan enemies
All of which just do not translate well into Serious Sam. Yes, we have reloading in previous games.... but only for the revolvers that are barely used once we acquire the tommy gun. Hit-scan enemies are also present. Ok sure, but only like 2 or 3 enemies not half of the entire roster. To makes matters worse, the infected helicopter enemy is hitscan and just flies above the player while also dodging rockets which are just too slow.
Most levels from SSTFE, SSTSE and SS2 are large, open spaces with tons of place to maneuver around enemy attacks and their projectiles. That's not the case in SS3 as, again, those are just destroyed cities in the Middle East with burned cars, destroyed bridges, barricades etc. scattered around. So dodging enemy attacks, especially hitscan enemies, can be very difficult with these assets blocking your path. 
Don't even get me started on the awful dark tomb sections with monkeys jumping from wall to wall.
The last level (excluding the final boss fight, which was alright) almost made me rip out hair from my head. It is genuinely one of the worst experiences I've had with any video game I've ever played. It's simply awful. Having every enemy from the entire game get respawned over and over and over again.... is just a terrible design.

The Soundtrack, as with other Serious Sam games, still slaps, so that's a plus.
All in all, while I do think it's a fine shooter in general, I would warn Serious Sam fans to not expect the same chaotic, mindless fun. Instead, get ready for a constant enemy spam, most of which are hitscan. 
Luckily, it has the workshop mod support in which you can find plenty of mods that get rid of the majority of annoying design choices, making it a better Serious Sam game.

When Serious Sam 3: BFE launched, a lot of people criticized it for being too slow, and many felt that aiming down sights and reloading had no place in a Serious Sam game. Personally, I think Serious Sam 3 strikes a great balance between modern FPS mechanics and the classic Serious Sam formula. That said, the game isn’t without its flaws. The biggest issue is the long stretch of interior levels, especially at the beginning of the campaign. These sections are slow, Sam’s movement feels sluggish, and they don’t capture the fast paced spirit that defines the series. They feel completely out of place compared to the outdoor levels. Once the game opens up, however, it becomes fantastic. Every outdoor level is brilliant and feels like a true evolution of the classic Serious Sam formula, delivering massive battlefields, huge enemy hordes, and nonstop action. The reloading mechanic is another minor downside, but the reload animations are so quick that they rarely become a problem during combat. The Jewel of the Nile DLC may be short, but it’s just as enjoyable as the main campaign, offering more of the intense action the series is known for. Serious Sam 3: BFE is a flawed, underrated gem that deserves far more appreciation than it receives. Without the slow opening, the lengthy interior sections, and the unnecessary reloading mechanic, it could have been a true masterpiece like TFE. Even so, I never disliked it the way many players did. It’s still an excellent Serious Sam game, and I highly recommend it to both longtime fans of the series and newcomers looking for a modern take on the classic old school shooter formula. 7/10

Some view it as the black sheep of the franchise. For me, it's a fantastic return to form after a 6 year-long wait. Responsive, fine gunplay combined with solid encounter design and fun new variations on existing enemies, all bringing Serious Sam into the modern world, and away from the Antiquity of FE and SE or the alien worlds of 2. 

A stronger melee weapon provides you with opportunities to save ammo. Instant melee kill execution moves do the same and give you additional options - though not as finely tuned as Doom's Glory Kills, they are a great way to provide breather room in a fight. Reloading and sprinting add micro-management and strategic resource and time management to the mix, making players think and keep track of their magazine in combat. The end result is an excellent mix between the old-school FPS traditions and newer inspirations from modern shooters - predating the Doom reboot by 5 years.

The story is nothing to write home about, but it's more naturalistic and somber than 2 and is present, unlike FE/SE. The soundtrack is, as always, a Croatian masterpiece combining heavy, drum-pounding rock with Eastern percussion and wind instruments. Although the opening levels can be a bit of a pain and have some imperfect level design, the rest of the game is a fantastic romp and incredibly fun. Seize the day and enjoy Serious Sam 3: BFE, because clearly id Software loved it so much they decided to make their own, with Doom 2016.

I completely felt like Croteam lost their way with it, and forgot that what made original SS games stand out was the fact that they went against the industry norm at the time, and did something fresh. With SS3 not only did they repeat most of what the older games did without building on it, they also added a whole bunch of unoriginal elements copied from modern shooters. Simply put, this is a boring game because it doesn't do anything new as a SS game or as an FPS Action game. I only got half way through it back in 2013, and then started playing it over in 2016 thinking maybe I just wasn't in the right mood to enjoy it back then, but that wasn't the case. I only managed to finish it by forcing my self to play it, and only because I couldn't stand not finishing a Sam game. Serious Sam 2 gets ragged on by SS fans a lot, but it's a much more fun game then this. 
 
Anyway, I post this review in hopes that maybe it will have some kind of influence over SS4, which I am very much anticipating. I hope Croteam realizes that SS formula has been copied and improved on in recent years, by games like Shadow Warrior (2013) and the new Doom, which means they have to do a lot more then build a same game with new levels and better graphics. People forget how influential first SS game actually was, it took the FPS games out of the scripted corridors and put the focus back on fun, Painkiller and the new Doom would not be games they are if it wasn't for Serious Sam. Serious Sam 4 needs to feel fresh again, just like FE did all those years ago.

Serious Sam is a thing....   

Yeah I honestly don't know much about the lineage of this game, I think I bought it in 2011 christmas steam sale and never got around to playing it. 

In all seriousness (pardon that pun) I don't know much about the game series.  However Serious sam was billed as being a shooter, and oh god yes, it's that.   However this isn't the modern military shooter.  No Serious sam is a shooter in the same way the original Doom was a shooter.  Take entirely too many enemies (And if doom had too many enemies, this game has obscene levels, but we'll get to that).  And no real cover system (other than standing behind columns or buildings while enemies rush you) and sweet ass weapons (another thing I need to touch upon) and just throws everything at the player.  

This is a pure adrenaline game,  You have levels that are expected to last about 60 minutes or so, and the player is tasked to get through them to progress a rudimentary story.  However I will say the story is somewhat interesting if not amazing.  Sam is exploring Egypt to try to rescue a scientist, which turns into a typical FPS story, find artifacts and explore the time-lock.   There's reasons but really what the story is doing is pushing you to go murder hundreds of enemies.  But it's not obscenely bad, it just is almost an after thought. 

However what IS done well is the level design.  The entire game has mostly an egyptian theme to it, there's a few levels in a city, and the final level... well let me get there.   But most levels are "egyptian" and while many of them are similar, each one is unique.   In fact this is far better than I expected.  It's a shooty bang bang game, but done competently well, where level design is really really good for the most part.  There's a few areas that are large and the player will get lost in it for a few minutes, but there's not a wealth of exits, and most areas really have two directions to go (one of which they've already been through). 

This is the same team that designed Talos Principle and I bring that up because Talos Principle is a decent game that shines with level design.   Serious Sam is the same way.  A good game that has shockingly great level design.  (until the last level) 

So really what Serious Sam 3 is, is a call back to simpler time.  No regenerating health, no excessive story, just a doom style shooter which throws tons of enemies at the player to wade through.  Each level has hundreds of enemies but the player has the tools to murder all of them.  This all adds up to a rather solid game. 

Until that final level.  Now I had a blast playing Serious Sam 3.  Everything was going great, and then I reached the final level.  Again everything starts out good, but in the statistics screen it said there's 1700 enemies in the level.  A bit of a red flag but it's the final level, it's going to be hard, and the level before I think had over a thousand enemies.  So far so good. 

The problem is the final level is weak.  For a game that had great design great skill and really unique touches to it.  The game shelves all that and gives the player a curving canyon that goes on for miles.  A couple ammo dumps, unlimited rocket boxes and just an obscene slog through the enemies.  I mean this isn't like the rest of the game that has these huge encounters, instead it's just "here's 100" enemies, go kill them.  

Ok that works for the most part, it's really fun to tear hundreds of weak enemies apart now that you have all the cool weapons, and that part isn't so bad.    But the level continues, near the end, the game just says "Screw it" and throws at least 10 of the Khnum (I think that's the spelling) enemies.  Now these guys are like the Hell Demon difficulty enemies in Doom, with the designs of the cyber demon.   But 10 of these guys are hard as hell and they keep coming.  At the same time you get other enemies (a couple hundred of them) that just charge and melee the player.  This is just a balls hard section of the game and the only way to really play it is to keep backing up and shooting rockets.  This section of the game, starts out with "large scale battle" and just become a depressing slog.  A lot of backpedalling, restocking and running back to shoot more enemies.  It's ... everything bad that the game hasn't been to that point. 

And then the final boss appears.  What could be an interesting boss ... well let's just say it's more an annoyance than a great boss fight. 

But does the last level ruin the game?  Well A bit.  I mean I like the game a lot but that level leaves a bad taste in the mouth.    But does it mean I can't recommend the game?  

Hell no.  In fact I really think I love this game.  It can be brutally hard (I played on easy after the first level on normal was a touch annoying)   It can be long (levels that take 45 minutes are the norm.)   And it can be fun... A LOT of fun.  

But there's one other thing I feel the need to talk about.  "Tourist" difficulty.  If this game is too hard you can turn this on.   In fact the wiki talks about much of the changes in difficulty for this game, and each difficulty has a really interesting series of changes, and the game definitely does feel like it does difficulty right.   That's really nice to see.

So overall I can highly recommend this game, and just warn people that the last level isn't as good as the rest of this absolute blast of the game.  This is a high octane amazing ride for anyone to play.  Definitely worth a pickup or a look for those sick of the same old military shooter.

Beyond all that, the game, for large portions of time, just doesn't feel like a Serious Sam, with it's modern military aesthetic, and the generic looking early levels. It only really starts to feel like one until about halfway through. It feels like a parody of the type of shooter that gaming webcomics like VG Cats would've made fun of back in the day.

Despite how negative this review sounds, again, it's really not a bad game, there is some fun to be had, namely through mods that add things like custom weapons. It's just, like I said, it's a mediocre game, and as such, I can't really recommend it, except maybe if it's on sale, especially to any potential newcomers to the series. I'd recommend the classics or Serious Sam HD or even the ever-divisive Serious Sam 2 over this game. I can only really recommend it to fans who really want a Sam fix without replaying the other games or people who want to mess around with mods.

- Pretty generic and lackluster visuals, with dust frequently blinding the player to nearby enemies (something that could not have been intentional)
- Annoying, dark, underground sections that resemble a bad horror game
- Terrible new enemies (with way too many hitscanners) and notable holes in the Serious Sam arsenal
- Some shocking performance issues, even with modern hardware

Serious Sam has been the epitome of ridiculously gory and crazy co-op gameplay for pretty much 20 years. Stunning graphics with intense amount of blood and gore along the game. Almost every aspect of the graphics beautifully made in this game. The only downside was the crude animation when the characters speak.

I love the soundtracks ! It really fits your situation in the game and the music changes each time you're in a new situation.

It's hard to give a review of this game. On one hand, if you compare it to First/Second Encounter, Serious Sam 3 is a disappointment. On the other hand, if you compare it to other shooters in general, it's still a lot of fun to play.

After SS2, Croteam looked at the mixed reception of the over-the-top cartoony approach and took the ball to the other side of the field, making Serious Sam 3 a gritty "realistic" modern military shooter that mostly sticks by the book. This unfortunately makes the game pretty boring to look at, with a drab color palette and lifeless scenery. The fun and quirky secrets from past Serious Sam games are mostly gone as well, replaced by simple ammo/health drops that are harder to see due to them not being floating pickups anymore.

So, is the gameplay still good? For the most part yes, but it comes with its share of caveats. The iconic Tommy Gun has been replaced with a standard boring assault rifle that needs to reload every few seconds, slowing down the action. The laser gun is MIA and doesn't appear outside of secrets until the expansion, Jewel of the Nile. The game also has a lot of enemies who unfortunately have hitscan weapons, meaning you'll often be taking damage you can't avoid. In previous games, the scorpion enemies would be few in number and make a sound a few seconds before opening fire, whereas in this game hitscan enemies are much more numerous and often get the drop on you. Additionally, there are some long underground puzzle sections with little to no gunplay that only serve to slow the game down.

The rest of it however is the same frantic Serious Sam action the series is known for, and if you can forgive it for its faults, you'll find Serious Sam 3 to be a satisfying, if not flawed old-school romp.
